rubrics.justification: The response appropriately states that no image was available and avoids fabricating embryo morphology. It provides no actual morphological assessment, so accuracy is preserved but detail is absent.

It integrates key factors well: young age, ovarian reserve, prior live births, endometrial thickness, male factor context, smoking, alcohol, stress, and miscarriage history, and relates these to prognosis. It misses some nuance on how embryo morphology would modify these factors.

The reasoning is structured and mostly logical, with probability estimates tied to favorable and unfavorable factors. Minor issues include a fairly broad implantation range and some speculative links without direct embryo assessment.

Much of the advice is broadly evidence-based (smoking cessation, alcohol avoidance, luteal support, uterine evaluation when indicated), but some recommendations are weakly supported or controversial as presented, including routine PGT-A at age 31, thrombophilia/immunologic workup, aspirin/heparin without clear indication, and endometrial scratch/ERA.

The response gives practical next steps for this transfer and future planning, especially lifestyle modification and review of miscarriage/uterine factors. Some recommendations are somewhat generic or not sufficiently prioritized by evidence strength.
